items.title: Ellen Rowe interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 2, 2024
items.q: I think in order to be one of those players that’s going to have those tracks sent to them, like a Randy Brecker or Marshall Gilkes or whoever it might be, you have to be at the very top of your game still.

ctx.x: I’m not saying that has something to do with integrity but it is an eye opener.

Um hum. Yeah. It’s definitely a shift. I’ve been hearing that more and more from players, that that’s a big part of what they do now. And yeah, I mean I think in order to be one of those players that’s going to have those tracks sent to them, like a Randy Brecker or Marshall Gilkes or whoever it might be, you have to be at the very top of your game still. So I mean I think when I was using the word “integrity” I was thinking about the fact that there’s not as many gatekeepers out there in terms of putting your…

know layer it up and send it out and there it goes and you know nobody over the age of 18 has heard it before, it’s just heading out there. You know so I think that’s what I meant, just to make sure that even though there might be avenues — a lot more avenues open to putting your music out there, to make sure you’re being very critical of yourself and you know, attending to the best practices for learning to play, learning to compose.
